name: Will-writing & probate (category guide)
summary: Singapore wills vs CPF nomination for expats — when a solicitor beats an online template, resealing foreign grants, and bank freezes after death.
body: A Singapore will moves local bank, brokerage, and condo assets; it does not move CPF — that needs a separate CPF nomination (or Public Trustee distribution if none exists). Online templates are weak for cross-border assets, minor guardianship, or foreign marriage/divorce histories; budget a solicitor consult when those apply. After death, Singapore banks usually freeze accounts until they see a Singapore grant of probate or letters of administration — a home-country grant alone often needs resealing or a fresh local application. Keep an asset list and executor contacts where your next-of-kin can find them; embassy repatriation logistics are a parallel rail. Pair will-writing with lasting power of attorney / advance medical directive planning while capacity is clear. Notary and apostille services help authenticate documents for foreign courts but do not replace a Singapore-qualified draftsman. This is a category guide, not a ranked firm list — verify counsel against the Ministry of Law directory and read CPF nomination rules yourself.
whenToEngage: Need Singapore will plus separate CPF nomination
Cross-border assets / minor guardianship — template unsafe
Foreign probate may not unfreeze local bank accounts
Executor / asset list missing for next-of-kin
